title: TPA overview (cloud)
description: Home: what is wrong now in each project (TPA first), the way through beta, the databases, the synthetic journeys and the scheduled runs, read from Cloud Monitoring. Every panel reads Cloud Monitoring metrics: Google's own, and the log-based counters tpa-platform's catalogue defines, whose labels are a closed list. No panel reads a log line.

panels.title: Now: what is wrong, by project (TPA first)
TPA · portal and sign-in
panels.description: The last 15 minutes in this project, one tile per problem, named: 5xx answers, uptime and inside checks failing (beta's checks pass on IAP's sign-in page), synthetic journeys failed or broken, crashes, out-of-memory kills, failed job runs, minutes the database was down. '✓ portal and sign-in · reporting' (teal) says this project's metrics are arriving (for the portal, the uptime checks' results; elsewhere, the database's own points); alone, it is the all-clear. '? Can't tell': nothing arrived, or the query failed. Open incidents are in PagerDuty. Reads "paused" or "database stopped", in no colour, while `auth-db` is stopped on purpose (the service's TPA_PAUSED_JOBS, TPA_STOPPED_DATABASES).

options.content:
**Open incidents are in PagerDuty**, not here: [PagerDuty incidents](https://app.pagerduty.com/incidents). Every Cloud Monitoring alert policy in a TPA project pages through it (urgent ones as high urgency). Google's own list, per project: [app](https://console.cloud.google.com/monitoring/alerting/incidents?project=__TPA_APP_PROJECT_ID__) · [member records](https://console.cloud.google.com/monitoring/alerting/incidents?project=__TPA_PHI_PROJECT_ID__) · [CRM](https://console.cloud.google.com/monitoring/alerting/incidents?project=__TPA_CRM_PROJECT_ID__).

This site reads metrics only: Grafana's Cloud Monitoring datasource cannot list incidents. Every panel reads Cloud Monitoring metrics: Google's own, and the log-based counters tpa-platform's catalogue defines, whose labels are a closed list. No panel reads a log line.

panels.title: Uptime checks passing (24 h)
panels.description: Share of uptime checks that passed in the last 24 h, by host. @@E@@Each check reads `/health` on a public host (the portal, auth and api hosts) from three US regions: a pass is the service answering through the load balancer and Cloud Armor. An outage pages when more than one region fails.@@Beta's hosts are behind IAP, so a check passes only on Google's sign-in page: it proves the address, the certificate, Cloud Armor and IAP, never the service behind them (that is the 5xx and instance panels). An outage pages when more than one region fails.@@

panels.title: Synthetic journeys (1 h)
panels.description: Each journey's runs in the last hour, by outcome (`synthetic_results`, one result line per run): `synthetics-staff-sign-in` (J1 staff sign-in): the portal, auth and a desk read that reaches tpa-db; `synthetics-ops-desk` (J2 ops desk): the ops host, auth and the live queue in svc-ops; `synthetics-crm` (J3 CRM sign-in): the CRM's own sign-in. pass is teal; fail is red (`synthetic-failing` pages on two fails and no pass in eleven minutes; J1 and J2 urgent); error is amber (the runner itself broke: `synthetic-broken`); skipped, grey. No runs at all: the journeys are off or paused (`synthetic-blind` when one goes quiet 15 minutes).

panels.title: Beta, left to right: the way in → web → tpa-api → auth and records → their databases
portal · ops (15 m)
panels.description: The way in: the share of uptime checks that passed in the last 15 minutes, by host. @@E@@Each check reads `/health` on a public host (the portal, auth and api hosts) from three US regions: a pass is the service answering through the load balancer and Cloud Armor. An outage pages when more than one region fails.@@Beta's hosts are behind IAP, so a check passes only on Google's sign-in page: it proves the address, the certificate, Cloud Armor and IAP, never the service behind them (that is the 5xx and instance panels). An outage pages when more than one region fails.@@

panels.title: inside (15 m)
panels.description: Private uptime checks (D-149): Google's VPC checkers read auth's and tpa-api's /ready at their internal load balancers; tpa-api's /ready asks records, so records is covered from inside too. The share that passed in the last 15 minutes, by service. auth's leaves while auth-db is stopped on purpose. None: the inside checks are off (private_uptime_checks_enabled).
